title: 6 VOLUMES OF 'AUSTRALIA IN THE...
reason: Complete run of Bean volumes I to VI plus a Light Horse title and The Little Black Princess; combined value may reach a few hundred dollars if the editions are early.
findings: Ten books. (1) C.E.W. Bean, Official History of Australia in the War of 1914-18, volumes I to VI (spines: I and II The Story of Anzac, III The AIF in France 1916, IV 1917, V and VI The AIF in France 1918), maroon cloth with gilt, Angus & Robertson at the foot of the spines; edition/printing not shown. (2) Modern Crusaders: With the Light Horse through Sinai and Palestine, orange cloth, clean cover (author W.S. Kent Hughes and a 1919 first edition per a dealer listing seen in search results 19/10/2026; not shown on the cover photo). (3) The Little Black Princess by Jeannie Gunn, green pictorial cloth; title page reads 'The Little Black Princess: A True Tale of Life in the Never-Never Land by Jeannie Gunn', no imprint or date photographed, so first edition status is unproven (a similar green cloth Robertson & Mullens 1925 copy was seen asking about US$50 on eBay). (4) A Book of Beauty in a red dust jacket. (5) Tasmanian Literary Landmarks (Giordano and Norman), inscribed 'To Mollie - best wishes, Margaret Giordano' (co-author, minor value).
condition: Bean volumes look clean with sound spines and bright gilt. Modern Crusaders cover clean with light toning. The Little Black Princess spine worn and corners bumped. A Book of Beauty jacket chipped and worn. Tasmanian Literary Landmarks is a paperback in fair order. Internal condition of all books unseen.
rescore_note: The Little Black Princess looks like the 1905 Alexander Moring first edition (title page wording by Jeannie Gunn and pictorial light green cloth match; an Australian dealer asks $1,200 for a worn copy, kaycraddock.com, seen 19/10/2026, but the imprint was not photographed), plus Bean vols I to VI and Modern Crusaders; my estimate $400 to 700 if the first edition holds, about $250 if not.
